# boopada

Goal: Build Boopada, a trip planner, one task per session.

Standing constraints — obey verbatim (4):
- [D1] Every money value in the API, in and out, is { amount_minor: integer, currency }; convert provider QuotedPrice via lib/money.ts, never via parseFloat.
- [D2] Interests are only provider activity categories (lib/categories.ts ACTIVITY_CATEGORIES); reject anything else with 400.
- [D3] Add schema changes only as a new entry appended to MIGRATIONS in lib/server/db.ts; never edit an applied migration.
- [D6] Never hard-delete traveller-made data: delete through softDelete() in lib/server/deletions.ts, and filter `deleted_at IS NULL` in every list, total and suggestion query.
Progress: 2/2 tasks done (100%) across 1 phase(s)

Phases:
- Roadmap [active — all tasks done; mark phase done?] 2/2
  - [x] S1 Traveller profile, and the roadmap

We're building Boopada, a trip planner. Here's the roadmap so you have the
whole picture. We'll go roughly in this order, one piece per session:

1. Traveller profile (today).
2. Bucket list: places and experiences to save for later.
3. Trips: create a trip from legs of cities and nights, with a draft day-by-day
   plan.
4. Itinerary editing: add, move and remove activities and days.
5. Itinerary view: the trip laid out day by day, with daily and trip totals.
6. Location to-dos: to-dos per day, surfaced when you arrive somewhere.
7. Activity suggestions and local transport costs.
8. Curation advisor: tells you what could be better and can fix it for you.
9. Chat: a command box on the trip page. It understands exactly these commands:
   - "add <activity name> to day <n>"
   - "remove <activity name> from day <n>"
   - "undo"
   - "make day <n> lighter": apply the advisor's lighten suggestion for that
     day, or remove that day's longest activity if there isn't one
   - "interest add <category>" / "interest remove <category>"
   - "what can be better": list the advisor's suggestions
   POST /api/chat { trip_id, message } returns
   { reply, changed, suggestions? }. Anything else gets a reply listing the
   commands, with changed: false.

Today: the traveller profile.

- GET /api/profile and PUT /api/profile with: home_currency, home_airport,
  cabin_class (economy | premium_economy | business | first),
  daily_activity_budget (optional), interests.
- Before anything is saved, GET returns home_currency USD, home_airport SFO,
  cabin_class economy, no budget, no interests.
- Validate: currency and airport must be ones the providers know.
- A /profile page to view and edit it (data-testid: profile-form,
  profile-save).

Two decisions to keep for the whole project:
- Money, everywhere in the API, going in and coming out, is
  { "amount_minor": integer, "currency": "ISO code" } in the currency's minor
  units: JPY and VND have none, JOD has three. No decimal strings, no floats.
  Our prototype used decimal strings and totals drifted.
- Interests are not free text. They're the providers' activity categories:
  culture, food, nature, adventure, nightlife, wellness, tour. Reject anything
  else.

Conventions for this project:
- Monorepo, bun. The app is apps/web (Next.js). Data providers come from
  @workspace/providers; use its fixture bundle.
- Storage: SQLite at the path in BOOPADA_DB_PATH (default ./data/boopada.sqlite).
  Create or upgrade the schema automatically on startup.
- Time: the current time is BOOPADA_NOW (ISO timestamp) when set, otherwise the
  system clock.
- API: JSON under /api. Errors return 4xx with { "error": { "code", "message" } }.
- One traveller, no login.
- The app must run with `bun run build`, then `bun run start` in apps/web
  (port from PORT).
- Before you finish, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test` pass.
- You may add features or improvements you judge valuable beyond the task.
  Record what you added and why.
  - [x] S2 Bucket list

Next: the bucket list.

- POST /api/bucket { title, city_id?, notes?, estimated_daily_spend? } returns
  the item with an id and created_at. GET /api/bucket returns { items }.
  PATCH /api/bucket/{id} edits. DELETE /api/bucket/{id} deletes.
- Unknown city_id is a 400.
- A /bucket page listing items, with add and delete (data-testid: bucket-item-{id},
  bucket-add, bucket-delete-{id}).

A decision for the whole app, not just this feature: we never hard-delete
anything the traveller made, and we don't ask "are you sure?". Deleting is a
soft delete, and POST /api/undo restores the most recent deletion (409 with
code "nothing_to_undo" when there's nothing). Deleted things never show up in
any list, total or suggestion.

# Plan: boopada

Goal: Build Boopada, a trip planner, one task per session.

Progress: 2/2 tasks done (100%)

## Roadmap [active] — 2/2 done

- [x] S1 Traveller profile, and the roadmap

We're building Boopada, a trip planner. Here's the roadmap so you have the
whole picture. We'll go roughly in this order, one piece per session:

1. Traveller profile (today).
2. Bucket list: places and experiences to save for later.
3. Trips: create a trip from legs of cities and nights, with a draft day-by-day
   plan.
4. Itinerary editing: add, move and remove activities and days.
5. Itinerary view: the trip laid out day by day, with daily and trip totals.
6. Location to-dos: to-dos per day, surfaced when you arrive somewhere.
7. Activity suggestions and local transport costs.
8. Curation advisor: tells you what could be better and can fix it for you.
9. Chat: a command box on the trip page. It understands exactly these commands:
   - "add <activity name> to day <n>"
   - "remove <activity name> from day <n>"
   - "undo"
   - "make day <n> lighter": apply the advisor's lighten suggestion for that
     day, or remove that day's longest activity if there isn't one
   - "interest add <category>" / "interest remove <category>"
   - "what can be better": list the advisor's suggestions
   POST /api/chat { trip_id, message } returns
   { reply, changed, suggestions? }. Anything else gets a reply listing the
   commands, with changed: false.

Today: the traveller profile.

- GET /api/profile and PUT /api/profile with: home_currency, home_airport,
  cabin_class (economy | premium_economy | business | first),
  daily_activity_budget (optional), interests.
- Before anything is saved, GET returns home_currency USD, home_airport SFO,
  cabin_class economy, no budget, no interests.
- Validate: currency and airport must be ones the providers know.
- A /profile page to view and edit it (data-testid: profile-form,
  profile-save).

Two decisions to keep for the whole project:
- Money, everywhere in the API, going in and coming out, is
  { "amount_minor": integer, "currency": "ISO code" } in the currency's minor
  units: JPY and VND have none, JOD has three. No decimal strings, no floats.
  Our prototype used decimal strings and totals drifted.
- Interests are not free text. They're the providers' activity categories:
  culture, food, nature, adventure, nightlife, wellness, tour. Reject anything
  else.

Conventions for this project:
- Monorepo, bun. The app is apps/web (Next.js). Data providers come from
  @workspace/providers; use its fixture bundle.
- Storage: SQLite at the path in BOOPADA_DB_PATH (default ./data/boopada.sqlite).
  Create or upgrade the schema automatically on startup.
- Time: the current time is BOOPADA_NOW (ISO timestamp) when set, otherwise the
  system clock.
- API: JSON under /api. Errors return 4xx with { "error": { "code", "message" } }.
- One traveller, no login.
- The app must run with `bun run build`, then `bun run start` in apps/web
  (port from PORT).
- Before you finish, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test` pass.
- You may add features or improvements you judge valuable beyond the task.
  Record what you added and why.
- [x] S2 Bucket list

Next: the bucket list.

- POST /api/bucket { title, city_id?, notes?, estimated_daily_spend? } returns
  the item with an id and created_at. GET /api/bucket returns { items }.
  PATCH /api/bucket/{id} edits. DELETE /api/bucket/{id} deletes.
- Unknown city_id is a 400.
- A /bucket page listing items, with add and delete (data-testid: bucket-item-{id},
  bucket-add, bucket-delete-{id}).

A decision for the whole app, not just this feature: we never hard-delete
anything the traveller made, and we don't ask "are you sure?". Deleting is a
soft delete, and POST /api/undo restores the most recent deletion (409 with
code "nothing_to_undo" when there's nothing). Deleted things never show up in
any list, total or suggestion.

Conventions for this project:
- Monorepo, bun. The app is apps/web (Next.js). Data providers come from
  @workspace/providers; use its fixture bundle.
- Storage: SQLite at the path in BOOPADA_DB_PATH (default ./data/boopada.sqlite).
  Create or upgrade the schema automatically on startup.
- Time: the current time is BOOPADA_NOW (ISO timestamp) when set, otherwise the
  system clock.
- API: JSON under /api. Errors return 4xx with { "error": { "code", "message" } }.
- One traveller, no login.
- The app must run with `bun run build`, then `bun run start` in apps/web
  (port from PORT).
- Before you finish, `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run test` pass.
- You may add features or improvements you judge valuable beyond the task.
  Record what you added and why.

Active phase: Roadmap
Next action: All planned roadmap tasks are done (2/2). The operator should add the next task to the plan; any new traveller-made entity must register in SOFT_DELETE_TABLES and filter deleted_at IS NULL.

rule: Interests are only provider activity categories (lib/categories.ts ACTIVITY_CATEGORIES); reject anything else with 400.

== shard decisions/D3.md (717 bytes) ==
<!-- generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl -->

D3 — 2026-09-15
rule: Add schema changes only as a new entry appended to MIGRATIONS in lib/server/db.ts; never edit an applied migration.
chose: SQLite through a thin adapter (lib/server/sqlite.ts): bun:sqlite under Bun (bun test), node:sqlite under Node (next start on Node 24); schema versioned with PRAGMA user_version migrations run when the DB opens, and instrumentation.ts opens it at server startup
over: better-sqlite3 (native addon build) or forcing next start onto the Bun runtime
because: No native dependency, works in both the test runner and the production server, and both built-ins share the prepare/get/all/run subset.

== shard decisions/D4.md (483 bytes) ==
<!-- generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl -->

D4 — 2026-09-15
chose: PUT /api/profile merges: omitted fields keep their current value, daily_activity_budget: null clears the budget; the whole body is validated before anything is written
over: strict full replacement requiring every field
because: Lets clients (and the future chat "interest add/remove") update one field without re-sending the rest, while still never saving a half-valid profile.

== shard decisions/D5.md (921 bytes) ==
<!-- generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl -->

D5 — 2026-09-15
chose: Beyond spec: profile responses carry updated_at (null until first save, from the BOOPADA_NOW-aware clock); errors add an optional `field` and specific codes (unknown_currency, unknown_airport, invalid_interest, validation_error, invalid_json, invalid_body); lib/money.ts ships quotedToMoney/decimalToMinor/formatMoney for later features; /profile has per-interest checkboxes (data-testid profile-interest-<category>) and a profile-status line; biome now ignores .sofar and .mcp.json
over: bare spec fields and a generic error code
because: Specific codes let the UI and tests tell failures apart; updated_at exercises the clock convention; the money helpers stop later sessions reinventing float-prone conversion; .mcp.json was unformatted at baseline and .sofar/.index is sofar-generated, both broke `bun run lint`.

== shard decisions/D6.md (1072 bytes) ==
<!-- generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl -->

D6 — 2026-09-15
rule: Never hard-delete traveller-made data: delete through softDelete() in lib/server/deletions.ts, and filter `deleted_at IS NULL` in every list, total and suggestion query.
chose: App-wide soft delete: traveller-made rows get a nullable deleted_at; every deletion appends to a `deletions` log (entity_type, entity_id, deleted_at, restored_at); POST /api/undo restores the newest unrestored log entry (a stack, so repeated undos walk back), 409 nothing_to_undo when none. New deletable types register their table in SOFT_DELETE_TABLES in apps/web/lib/server/deletions.ts and go through softDelete().
over: hard DELETE, confirmation dialogs, per-table undo, or an undo that only remembers a single last deletion
because: Operator decision for the whole app (never hard-delete, no "are you sure?", undo restores the most recent deletion). One log works across entity types added later, and a stack means undo still makes sense after several deletes.
guard: cmd:*DELETE FROM*

== shard decisions/D7.md (969 bytes) ==
<!-- generated by sofar — do not hand-edit; truth lives in events.jsonl -->

D7 — 2026-09-15
chose: Bucket API shape: integer ids; POST 201 returns { id, title, city_id, notes, estimated_daily_spend: Money|null, created_at, updated_at }; GET lists live items newest first; PATCH merges (omitted keeps, null clears optional fields); DELETE is 204; PATCH/DELETE on missing, deleted or non-integer ids is 404 not_found; unknown city_id is 400 unknown_city (city checked via providers.locale.getCity); title is trimmed, 1–200 chars; notes ≤5000 chars, blank becomes null; the spend currency must be one the providers know (unknown_currency). Undo response: { restored: { type, item } }.
over: bare spec fields without updated_at/validation codes, or strict PATCH replacement
because: This matches the S1 profile conventions (merge semantics, field-specific codes, D1 money), and deleted items act as if they don't exist, as the operator's delete decision requires.

chose: Beyond spec: the /bucket page has an inline "Deleted X · Undo" bar (data-testid bucket-undo-bar / bucket-undo) that calls POST /api/undo, plus city select, daily-spend input defaulting to the profile home currency, and notes; home page links to /bucket; .gitignore now covers *.sqlite-wal and *.sqlite-shm (WAL mode left them untracked-but-visible).
